title: Forward Deployed Engineering at Cursor — Pauline Brunet

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling

summary: Pauline Brunet leads the global forward deployed engineering (FDE) team at Cursor. She frames FDE placement around a two-axis matrix: customer digital maturity (low to high) and product customization (low to high). High-maturity, low-customization customers should get self-service with good documentation—not FDE. Low-maturity, low-customization is traditional SaaS deployment—also not FDE. High-maturity, high-customization is where FDEs act as advisers to accelerate adoption. Low-maturity, high-customization is where FDEs drive embedded transformation because those customers cannot hire or staff the needed talent themselves. The FDE role spans working with CIOs, CTOs, COOs, VPs of AI, developers, and engineering managers—leading discovery, finding use cases, understanding processes and culture, and accompanying the customer through change. FDEs must stay at the cutting edge of technology and maintain a feedback loop between product and engineering teams. Cursor engagements are project-based, scoped with the economic buyer to ensure strategic alignment, meaningful ROI, and customer resourcing. Cursor FDEs deploy cloud agents, long-running agents, automations, and SDK-built applications. They co-develop in customer codebases and push edge-case use cases beyond the SDLC into HR, finance, supply chain, and e-commerce. Staff augmentation is a red flag. The team currently hires very technical people with customer-facing experience—not new graduates—but plans to split the role over time into less technical/more customer-facing and highly technical/less customer-ready profiles. The organization is geography-based now but will mature to industry verticals because industry credibility requires using the right lingo. Dedicated SMEs cover product areas like long-running cloud agents and the Cursor SDK. Best practices include learning quickly and pivoting, listening to customers for new offerings, partnering with system integrators and consultants for change management and scale, saying no when Cursor is not the right tool to build trust, and attracting and paying top talent. Engagement tips: verify you are solving the right problem with the right person, define success from the start, keep scope directional over roughly six weeks, involve the customer in every step, measure success against baselines, and communicate ROI—which always reduces to increasing revenue, decreasing costs, or mitigating risk. Leave documentation artifacts behind and hire A players.

sections.title: Introduction and background
sections.summary: Pauline Brunet introduces herself as leader of the global FDE team at Cursor, with 10 years of enterprise AI deployment experience across consulting and three tech companies. She frames the talk around learnings from building the FDE function.

sections.title: The FDE matrix: when and when not to deploy
sections.summary: Pauline presents a two-axis matrix: customer digital maturity versus product customization. FDE is not appropriate for high-maturity/low-customization (self-service) or low-maturity/low-customization (traditional SaaS). FDE earns its place in high-maturity/high-customization (advisory acceleration) and low-maturity/high-customization (embedded transformation). She warns against using FDEs for training sessions, bug writing, or documentation updates.

sections.title: What the FDE job entails
sections.summary: The FDE role requires working across all organizational levels—from CIOs and CTOs to developers—leading discovery, finding use cases, understanding processes and culture, and accompanying customers through change. FDEs must stay at the cutting edge of technology and maintain a feedback loop between product and engineering teams.

sections.title: Cursor FDE practice: ROI, co-development, and edge cases
sections.summary: Cursor FDE engagements are project-based, scoped with the economic buyer to ensure strategic alignment, meaningful ROI, and customer resourcing. Deployments include cloud agents, long-running agents, automations, and SDK applications. FDEs co-develop in customer codebases and push edge-case use cases beyond the SDLC into HR, finance, supply chain, and e-commerce. Staff augmentation requests are a red flag.

sections.title: FDE mission and team structure
sections.summary: Pauline shares Cursor's FDE mission: partner with organizations to co-design and co-build their AI software factory. The team hires highly technical, experienced unicorns—5+ year software engineers, not new graduates—matching profiles to Cursor's deeply technical buyer base.

sections.title: Team evolution: role splitting, industry verticals, and SMEs
sections.summary: The FDE team currently hires very technical people with customer-facing experience and no new graduates, but plans to split the role over time into less technical/more customer-facing and highly technical/less customer-ready profiles. The organization is geography-based now but will mature to industry verticals because using the wrong lingo immediately loses credibility. Dedicated SMEs cover product areas like long-running cloud agents and the Cursor SDK. Hires come from companies like Spotify, Rippling, and Palantir. The team expects roles and structure to change every six months as products and customer journeys evolve.

sections.title: Best practices: learn, listen, partner, and say no
sections.summary: Pauline shares best practices: learn quickly and pivot rather than over-plan; listen to customers—she is creating a new organizational-transformation offering after hearing the same request six or seven times; partner with system integrators and consultants who know the customers and can handle change management at scale; say no when Cursor is not the right tool to build credibility and trust; and attract and pay the right talent to stay competitive in the war for talent.

sections.title: Running FDE engagements: scope, involvement, and measurement
sections.summary: Engagement tips: verify you are solving the right problem with the right person; define success from the start with concrete baselines; keep scope directional—e.g., automate a process using long-running agents over six weeks—rather than open-ended staff augmentation; involve the customer in every step from scoping to ROI measurement; measure whether results hit the target and communicate ROI, which always reduces to increasing revenue, decreasing costs, or mitigating risk; and leave documentation artifacts behind.

sections.title: Wrap up: build trust and hire A players
sections.summary: Pauline closes by advising teams to build the right FDE motion for their company, learn and pivot and scale, create a culture where people want to do their best work, and hire A players—because B players hire C players.
